grf.hypothesis: Archiving the exact Git tree object instead of the commit object, with a genuinely fixed archive mtime, yields source bytes independent of commit identity/export-subst and reproducible across staging calls.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: Commit-object archive semantics or ambiguous mtime syntax can inject commit/time-dependent bytes even when the Git tree is unchanged.
grf.discriminator: Create two commits with the exact same tree and an export-subst path, compare commit-object archives, compare tree-object archives, then repeat the tree archive with an explicit ISO-8601 epoch mtime and verify extracted bytes against the Git blob.
grf.collapse: RETAIN tree-object plus explicit ISO-8601 fixed mtime; REJECT commit-object archive as tree-byte authority; REJECT --mtime=@0 as a validated fixed-epoch spelling in the measured Git 2.47.3 environment.

primary_evidence.finding: Archive behavior differs depending on whether the tree-ish is a commit/tag or a tree, and archive mtime can be overridden explicitly.
export-subst can substitute commit-derived placeholders during git archive, so commit-object archive bytes are not necessarily a pure function of the tree object.
